--- title: "Reading tabular data in R" author: "Dr. Adrian Correndo" date: "2026-01-21" format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 4 number-sections: true toc-location: left code-tools: true categories: files, csv, excel, spreadsheet, readr, readxl, openxlsx execute: echo: true eval: true editor: source --- # Introduction 📌 In real projects, a big part of “data science" is simply getting data into R reliably and reproducibly. CSV (comma separated values) and Excel are the most common formats you’ll see in agriculture, industry, and research workflows. This short note covers:
- 📄 how to read CSV (readr).
- 📊 how to read Excel (readxl, openxlsx).
- 🗂️ how to read many files in a folder.
- 🧾 how to read many sheets in an excel file.
- 🧹 common cleaning options like skipping rows, header rows, and missing values
# Libraries 📦 ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(pacman) p_load(dplyr, purrr, stringr, tibble) # data wrangling p_load(readr, readxl, openxlsx) # to read files ``` ::: ## Quick comparison of main packages 📄 CSV / delimited text - Package: readr - ✅ Strengths: fast, consistent parsing, clear messages, good type control (col_types) - ⚠️ Notes: great default for tidyverse-style workflows 📊 Excel (.xlsx) - Package: readxl - ✅ Strengths: simple reading of Excel, minimal dependencies - ⚠️ Notes: read-only (does not write Excel) 📊 Excel (.xlsx) - Package: openxlsx - ✅ Strengths: read + write, more control over excels/sheets - ⚠️ Notes: great when you must write .xlsx outputs Rule of thumb: - 📄 CSV: start with readr::read_csv() - 📊 Excel reading: start with readxl::read_excel() - 📝 Excel reading + writing or more control: use openxlsx # Reading CSV files 📄 ## Basic read ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df <- readr::read_csv("data/my_file.csv") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Rows: 289 Columns: 6 ── Column specification ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Delimiter: "," chr (4): gen, trial, env, loc dbl (2): yield, year ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data. ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message. ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} df ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 289 × 6 gen trial env yield year loc 1 G16 T2 E01 590 2001 Mieso 2 G17 T2 E01 554 2001 Mieso 3 G18 T2 E01 586 2001 Mieso 4 G19 T2 E01 738 2001 Mieso 5 G20 T2 E01 489 2001 Mieso 6 G21 T2 E01 684 2001 Mieso 7 G22 T2 E01 555 2001 Mieso 8 G23 T2 E01 1025 2001 Mieso 9 G24 T2 E01 493 2001 Mieso 10 G25 T2 E01 691 2001 Mieso # ℹ 279 more rows ``` ::: ::: ## Common options missing values, quieter output ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df <- readr::read_csv( file = "data/my_file.csv", na = c("", "NA", "N/A", "na", ".") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Rows: 289 Columns: 6 ── Column specification ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Delimiter: "," chr (4): gen, trial, env, loc dbl (2): yield, year ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data. ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message. ``` ::: ::: ## Control column types 🎯 Recommended for reproducibility. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df <- readr::read_csv(file = "data/my_file.csv") |> mutate(loc = as.character(loc), year = as.integer(year), yield = as.numeric(yield)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Rows: 289 Columns: 6 ── Column specification ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Delimiter: "," chr (4): gen, trial, env, loc dbl (2): yield, year ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data. ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message. ``` ::: ::: ## Skip lines at the top ⏭️ For example for metadata, notes, extra header rows... ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df <- readr::read_csv( file = "data/my_file.csv", skip = 1 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Rows: 288 Columns: 6 ── Column specification ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Delimiter: "," chr (4): G16, T2, E01, Mieso dbl (2): 590, 2001 ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data. ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message. ``` ::: ::: ## Skip blank lines 🕳️ Often helpful with messy CSV exports ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df <- readr::read_csv( file = "data/my_file.csv", skip_empty_rows = TRUE ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Rows: 289 Columns: 6 ── Column specification ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Delimiter: "," chr (4): gen, trial, env, loc dbl (2): yield, year ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data. ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message. ``` ::: ::: # Reading Excel files (.xlsx) 📊 ## Basic read (first sheet by default) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df <- readxl::read_excel(path="data/my_excel.xlsx") head(df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 6 gen trial env yield year loc 1 G16 T2 E01 590 2001 Mieso 2 G17 T2 E01 554 2001 Mieso 3 G18 T2 E01 586 2001 Mieso 4 G19 T2 E01 738 2001 Mieso 5 G20 T2 E01 489 2001 Mieso 6 G21 T2 E01 684 2001 Mieso ``` ::: ::: ## Read a specific sheet by name or position ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df1 <- readxl::read_excel(path="data/my_excel.xlsx", sheet = "Sheet1") df2 <- readxl::read_excel(path="data/my_excel.xlsx", sheet = 2) ``` ::: ## Skip rows ⏭️ For example, title row + empty row ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df <- readxl::read_excel( path = "data/my_excel.xlsx", sheet = 1, skip = 2 ) ``` ::: ## Diagnose 🔎 For example, "empty first row" or "headers" not where expected" ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df_rows <- readxl::read_excel( path = "data/my_excel.xlsx", sheet = 1, n_max = 6, # number of rows of data col_names = FALSE # remove headers row ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` New names: • `` -> `...1` • `` -> `...2` • `` -> `...3` • `` -> `...4` • `` -> `...5` • `` -> `...6` ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} df_rows ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 6 ...1 ...2 ...3 ...4 ...5 ...6 1 gen trial env yield year loc 2 G16 T2 E01 590 2001 Mieso 3 G17 T2 E01 554 2001 Mieso 4 G18 T2 E01 586 2001 Mieso 5 G19 T2 E01 738 2001 Mieso 6 G20 T2 E01 489 2001 Mieso ``` ::: ::: Then set skip based on what you see (commonly skip = 1 or skip = 2) and re-read. ## Reading Excel with openxlsx 🛠 Nice when you also write excel files later ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df_sr1 <- openxlsx::read.xlsx( xlsxFile = "data/my_excel.xlsx", sheet = 1, startRow = 1 # speficies where headers are located ) head(df_sr1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` gen trial env yield year loc 1 G16 T2 E01 590 2001 Mieso 2 G17 T2 E01 554 2001 Mieso 3 G18 T2 E01 586 2001 Mieso 4 G19 T2 E01 738 2001 Mieso 5 G20 T2 E01 489 2001 Mieso 6 G21 T2 E01 684 2001 Mieso ``` ::: ::: ### Skip rows by moving startRow ⏭️: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df_sr3 <- openxlsx::read.xlsx( xlsxFile = "data/my_excel.xlsx", sheet = 1, startRow = 3 ) slice_head(df_sr3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` G17 T2 E01 554 2001 Mieso 1 G18 T2 E01 586 2001 Mieso ``` ::: ::: # Reading multiple CSV files 🗂️ This is extremely common when we have one file per site, year, trial, etc. ## Read + stack 🧱 This is call row-bind ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} folder <- "data" files <- list.files(path = folder, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE) all_data <- files |> setNames(basename(files)) |> # here we name by file basename # Here we read and stack using map_dfr purrr::map_dfr( \(f) readr::read_csv(f), # here we read each file .id = "source_file" # this creates a new column with the file name ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Rows: 289 Columns: 6 ── Column specification ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Delimiter: "," chr (4): gen, trial, env, loc dbl (2): yield, year ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data. ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message. Rows: 289 Columns: 6 ── Column specification ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Delimiter: "," chr (4): gen, trial, env, loc dbl (2): yield, year ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data. ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message. ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} head(all_data) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 7 source_file gen trial env yield year loc 1 my_file_02.csv G16 T2 E01 590 2001 Mieso 2 my_file_02.csv G17 T2 E01 554 2001 Mieso 3 my_file_02.csv G18 T2 E01 586 2001 Mieso 4 my_file_02.csv G19 T2 E01 738 2001 Mieso 5 my_file_02.csv G20 T2 E01 489 2001 Mieso 6 my_file_02.csv G21 T2 E01 684 2001 Mieso ``` ::: ::: ## Add variables from filename 🏷️ For example year, or site ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} all_data <- files |> purrr::map_dfr( # here we read each file \(f) readr::read_csv(f) |> dplyr::mutate(source_file = basename(f)) ) |> # add filename as column dplyr::mutate(year = stringr::str_extract(source_file, "\\d{4}")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Rows: 289 Columns: 6 ── Column specification ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Delimiter: "," chr (4): gen, trial, env, loc dbl (2): yield, year ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data. ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message. Rows: 289 Columns: 6 ── Column specification ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Delimiter: "," chr (4): gen, trial, env, loc dbl (2): yield, year ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data. ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message. ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # here we extract a 4-digit year from the filename all_data %>% group_by(source_file) %>% slice_head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2 × 7 # Groups: source_file [2] gen trial env yield year loc source_file 1 G16 T2 E01 590 Mieso my_file.csv 2 G16 T2 E01 590 Mieso my_file_02.csv ``` ::: ::: ## Keep them as a named list 📚 ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} csv_list <- files |> setNames(basename(files)) |> purrr::map(\(f) readr::read_csv(f)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Rows: 289 Columns: 6 ── Column specification ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Delimiter: "," chr (4): gen, trial, env, loc dbl (2): yield, year ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data. ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message. Rows: 289 Columns: 6 ── Column specification ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Delimiter: "," chr (4): gen, trial, env, loc dbl (2): yield, year ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data. ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message. ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} names(csv_list) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "my_file_02.csv" "my_file.csv" ``` ::: ::: # Reading multiple Excel files 🗂️📊 ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} folder <- "data" files <- list.files(path = folder, pattern = "\\.xlsx$", full.names = TRUE) all_xlsx <- files |> purrr::map_dfr( \(f) readxl::read_excel(f, sheet = 1) |> # read first sheet from each dplyr::mutate(source_file = basename(f)) # add filename as column ) all_xlsx %>% group_by(source_file) %>% slice_head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2 × 7 # Groups: source_file [2] gen trial env yield year loc source_file 1 G16 T2 E01 590 2001 Mieso my_excel.xlsx 2 G16 T2 E01 590 2001 Mieso my_file_02.xlsx ``` ::: ::: # Reading multiple sheets 🧾🧾🧾 ## With readxl ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} path <- "data/my_excel.xlsx" sheets <- readxl::excel_sheets(path) all_sheets <- sheets |> setNames(sheets) |> purrr::map_dfr( \(sh) readxl::read_excel(path, sheet = sh) |> dplyr::mutate(sheet = sh) ) all_sheets %>% group_by(sheet) %>% slice_head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2 × 7 # Groups: sheet [2] gen trial env yield year loc sheet 1 G16 T2 E01 590 2001 Mieso Sheet1 2 G16 T2 E01 590 2001 Mieso Sheet2 ``` ::: ::: ## With openxlsx 🛠️ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} path <- "data/my_excel.xlsx" sheets <- openxlsx::getSheetNames(path) all_sheets <- sheets |> setNames(sheets) |> purrr::map_dfr( \(sh) openxlsx::read.xlsx(path, sheet = sh) |> dplyr::mutate(sheet = sh) ) all_sheets %>% group_by(sheet) %>% slice_head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2 × 7 # Groups: sheet [2] gen trial env yield year loc sheet 1 G16 T2 E01 590 2001 Mieso Sheet1 2 G16 T2 E01 590 2001 Mieso Sheet2 ``` ::: ::: ## Footnotes in Excel 📝 If a sheet has footnotes at the bottom, you can often remove them after import by filtering rows: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df <- readxl::read_excel(path="data/my_excel.xlsx") |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(yield)) # example: keep rows that have yield ``` ::: # Summary - Use readr::read_csv() for most CSV workflows (fast + consistent). - Use readxl::read_excel() for quick Excel imports. - Use openxlsx when you need more Excel control or want to write .xlsx outputs. - For multiple files or sheets, combine list.files()/excel_sheets() with purrr::map_dfr() to create one clean dataset.
